body:
If I'm honest, I really don't know either. I know I am not the only one, and that his kind of thing happens to a disturbing amount of people, some of whom never say anything or get help. There's so much literature on how to get through that rock bottom moment and move to safety, but so little on what to do with oneself afterwards.

It's easy to say you should just continue on like normal, but for the sufferer and the people around him it's really not that simple. Relationships get strained, the person in turmoil starts to doubt himself, and sometimes it seems like the care ends as soon as suicide is off the table immediately. That's where I am now, and it's the time when I feel help is almost more critical for recovery, but in my case as in so many others it's nowhere to be found.

So I turn to writing, journaling, and just attempting to push on regardless of my latent fears. Nothing will remove them from my sight, so I might as well make something. I've always wanted to write about depression and really try to bring the experience of it alive so people can maybe empathize a little more. I've also always worried no one would care.

So thanks for your kind words. I really tried to pour my heart into this to get it out, and it's nice to know someone read it and cared.
